transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-16
Start time: 14:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Ethan Chen (Redwood SE), Sofia Alvarez (Redwood SE), Laura Kim (Trident CISO), Rajesh Singh (Head Cloud Ops), Tomas Weber (Security Eng), Emily Park (Procurement)

00:00 Laura Kim: alright thanks everyone for joining, um we wanted to go through the SOC2 and ISO posture for Redwood before we move forward with procurement. we're on a tight timeline, internal vendor review due end of next week.
00:18 Maya Patel: great thanks Laura, yeah happy to run through that. quick intros - i'm Maya, i'm the AE, ethan and sofia are gonna handle the technical bits.
00:25 Ethan Chen: hey all, thanks. quick note, i'll focus on KMS and logs.
00:31 Rajesh Singh: good, our main concerns are encryption key control, audit log access and retention, and whether we can have a private deployment in our VPC if needed.
00:42 Maya Patel: totally understood. quick overview: we have a SOC 2 Type II report covering the hosted service, and we maintain ISO 27001 certification scope for the inference platform. we also have a trust center with artifacts and controls mapping for customers.
00:56 Tomas Weber: can you share the SOC 2 right away? we need the report to kick off procurement checks.
01:03 Maya Patel: yes i'll send the Type II report link after the call; it's in the trust center and we can give read-only access to Laura and Tomas.
01:12 Laura Kim: read-only is fine. also can you confirm whether the SOC cover includes dedicated and private deployments? sometimes the scope is limited.
01:22 Sofia Alvarez: good question. short answer: hosted inference is in scope for SOC 2 Type II; Dedicated and Private have a separate controls matrix - we can provide a mapping that shows which controls apply to each deployment model.
01:36 Rajesh Singh: ok we'll need that mapping, specifically for encryption at rest and key custody. our policy wants customer-managed keys for production PII workloads.
01:47 Ethan Chen: we support customer-managed KMS via integration with AWS KMS and GCP KMS, and for private deployments we can support HSM-backed keys. there's some config specifics we'll share.
01:58 Tomas Weber: how is the KMS integrated? is that a bring-your-own-key by default or do we host keys?
02:06 Ethan Chen: you can do either. by default Redwood-managed keys are used for hosted to simplify ops; for customers requiring BYOK we have a documented model where you provide a key or a key policy and we use the customer key for encryption. the trust center doc shows the architecture and crypto boundaries.
02:25 Laura Kim: and how do you prove key separation in the SOC2? does the attestation include key management controls?
02:33 Maya Patel: the SOC 2 scope includes cryptographic key management controls for hosted; the report includes control descriptions. for customer-managed keys, controls are captured in the controls mapping and we include guidance for customers to validate the configuration.
02:50 Rajesh Singh: audit logs - we need real time export to our SIEM, retention of 7 years for certain logs, and immutability guarantees. what do you offer?
03:03 Sofia Alvarez: audit logs are available via streaming export to S3 or PubSub and can be forwarded to SIEMs. retention defaults vary by plan but we can export full logs on demand. immutability is supported via write-once S3 buckets and we can provide hashes for integrity checks.
03:20 Tomas Weber: is there a native retention policy UI or is it manual?
03:24 Ethan Chen: there's a retention config param and we can set retention at the tenant level; for very long retention we recommend exporting to your own storage because hosted storage is optimized for operational retention.
03:39 Emily Park: for procurement we need a diagram of log flow and who has access to the logs.
03:45 Maya Patel: yes we'll include a diagram in the artifacts we share.
03:50 Laura Kim: SSO - we use Okta and need SAML + SCIM for provisioning and RBAC. does Redwood support SCIM?
03:58 Sofia Alvarez: yes we support SAML for SSO and SCIM for user provisioning, role mapping via our RBAC model. we can integrate with Okta and map idp groups to Redwood roles.
04:10 Rajesh Singh: are there builtin roles for auditors and do they get read-only access to logs and billing?
04:16 Ethan Chen: yes we have auditor role with read-only permissions including audit logs and billing views; fine-grained permissions can be configured via the console or APIs.
04:27 Laura Kim: data residency - we need assurance that data for EU customers remains in eu-west1 for example. how do you handle region pinning?
04:36 Maya Patel: you can pin workloads to regions; we support regional model routing and data residency controls in the control plane. for Private deployments the data stays in your network entirely.
04:47 Rajesh Singh: network isolation - does Redwood do VPC peering or private links?
04:51 Ethan Chen: we support VPC peering and private endpoints; for Dedicated we run in your VPC or in a dedicated tenant with network isolation.
05:00 Tomas Weber: any third-party dependencies that cause control gaps? we need to know subservice orgs for our vendor review.
05:07 Maya Patel: yes the trust center lists our subservice providers - e.g., cloud infra providers, monitoring, and some managed services. the SOC 2 report has a subservice appendix.
05:18 Laura Kim: one of our requirements is to see evidence of penetration testing and vulnerability management cadence.
05:24 Sofia Alvarez: we perform annual pen tests plus continuous vuln scanning; we can provide summary reports and remediation SLAs in the trust center.
05:35 Rajesh Singh: do you support FIPS crypto modules or HSMs for customers with higher compliance needs?
05:42 Ethan Chen: for private and Dedicated with HSM we can integrate with FIPS-validated HSMs in the cloud or customer HSMs on-prem. hosted default stack is industry-standard TLS and KMS; we can discuss FIPS on a case-by-case basis.
05:58 Laura Kim: ok procurement question: what are the timelines for onboarding and for doing a KMS POC?
06:05 Maya Patel: onboarding is typically 2-4 weeks for standard hosted, and Dedicated/private varies by environment complexity. KMS POC we can spin up a short sandbox and do a config in under a week.
06:16 Emily Park: from procurement we need the insurance certs and indemnity language too.
06:21 Maya Patel: noted, we'll add insurance and contract templates to the shared folder.
06:26 Tomas Weber: two more technical clarifications - does Redwood expose raw request/response logs with PII stripped? and what's the redaction model?
06:36 Sofia Alvarez: we redact at the application layer and provide configurable redaction policies; raw logs can be exported to customer-owned storage if needed but we recommend redaction plus pseudonymization.
06:49 Rajesh Singh: is there an option for on-prem inference where we keep full control?
06:54 Ethan Chen: yes private deployment is available - we ship a private control plane package and you can run inference in your VPC or on-prem hardware. that option is covered under enterprise licensing.
07:08 Laura Kim: control mapping - can you provide a spreadsheet that maps Redwood controls to our internal control IDs so our auditors can sign off quickly?
07:19 Maya Patel: yes we have a controls mapping template; we'll populate it with SOC/ISO controls and mapping to our features and provide guidance notes.
07:28 Tomas Weber: do you support automated evidence collection API for audits?
07:33 Sofia Alvarez: we have APIs and export endpoints for audit artifacts, evidence bundles, and we support read-only access to the trust center for auditors.
07:44 Rajesh Singh: pricing impact - if we require customer-managed keys and long retention exports, is there an additional cost?
07:52 Maya Patel: there can be additional charges for log egress and for Dedicated/private deployments; we'll include pricing notes in the follow-up.
08:01 Laura Kim: can you show where the controls mapping lives in the trust center?
08:05 Maya Patel: i will include screenshots and a link in the email.
08:10 Emily Park: timeline for next steps?
08:13 Maya Patel: i'll send artifacts by EOD monday, sofia and ethan will prep the KMS deep dive and diagrams, and we'll provision trust center access. propose next call for KMS deep dive on 2026-07-23.
08:27 Laura Kim: that works for us.
08:30 Tomas Weber: one last note - we may want a short security questionnaire answered (SIG, or BitSight?), do you do automated SIG export?
08:38 Sofia Alvarez: we can provide an exported SIG questionnaire and our answers; trust center includes a standard SIG fill.
08:45 Rajesh Singh: ok thanks everyone. we'll review the docs and set procurement timeline.
08:49 Maya Patel: thanks all, we'll follow up.

End of transcript
